title: Animal movement trajectory as a LineString
sql: JOIN species sp ON sp.species_id = a.species_id
JOIN sighting s ON s.animal_id = a.animal_id

steps.title: Filter animal and window
steps.text: Only sightings of animal 1 within the last 30 days are kept. Sightings 1, 2 and 3 qualify, the oldest being 25 days old. Sightings of other animals are rejected.

steps.title: Order points by time
steps.text: ORDER BY inside ST_MakeLine sorts the points chronologically before they are joined, so the line follows the real path.

steps.title: Require two points
steps.text: HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 drops animals with a single sighting, since one point cannot form a line.

steps.title: Select the window
steps.text: Sightings 1, 2 and 3 belong to animal 1 and fall within 30 days. The filter runs inside the CTE so the window function sees only relevant rows.

steps.title: Look back one row
steps.text: LAG returns the previous location in time order for the same animal. The first sighting has no predecessor, so its prev_location is NULL.

steps.title: Drop the first row
steps.text: The row without a previous point cannot form a leg, so it is removed. Two legs remain: sighting 1 to 2 and sighting 2 to 3.

steps.title: Sum the legs
steps.text: Each leg is about 1.54 km. Adding them gives the total path length in meters.

steps.title: Apply the time window
steps.text: All five incidents are newer than 30 days, so none is rejected. WHERE runs before the window function, so only these rows are clustered.

steps.title: Run k-means
steps.text: ST_ClusterKMeans groups the points into 2 clusters by location. The three North Zone incidents sit together and the two South Zone incidents form the other cluster. k must not exceed the number of rows, so a small k is used for this sample.

steps.title: Return cluster ids
steps.text: Every incident is returned together with its cluster number, which starts at 0.

title: Animals sighted in a zone in the last 7 days
sql: JOIN animal a ON a.animal_id = s.animal_id
JOIN species sp ON sp.species_id = a.species_id

steps.title: Zone filter
steps.text: The index on zone_id keeps sightings 1, 2, 3 and 6. Sightings 4 and 5 belong to South Zone.

steps.title: Time filter
steps.text: Sighting 1 is from October 12, far outside the 7 day window, so only sightings 2, 3 and 6 remain.

steps.title: Join and sort
steps.text: Each sighting is matched to its animal and species, and results are ordered newest first.

title: Species not sighted recently in a known zone
sql: JOIN animal a ON a.species_id = sp.species_id

steps.title: Find stale animals
steps.text: Animals 1, 2 and 3 were last updated more than a day ago. Animal 4 was updated this morning and is rejected.

steps.title: Check the last known area
steps.text: EXISTS only asks whether some zone polygon covers the animal's last position. SELECT 1 is enough because the subquery returns no columns that are used. All three animals lie inside a zone.

steps.title: Group by species
steps.text: Animals are counted per species and the latest update is kept with MAX.
